messages.subject: annotateWithGeneParts Vs GREAT for predicting function of genomic regions
parts:
Hello All,

 I am bit confused about the annotation function. I would really appreciate if someone can explain it to me.
 
 I am using annotateWithGeneParts to annotate the DMRs and using the gene IDs to do enrichment analysis. I have seen some published studies where GREAT (http://bejerano.stanford.edu/great/public/html/) is used to annoate and do the enrichment analysis. My question is 1) Are they both one and the same? The reason I am asking is I work with zebrafish and GREAT website still uses older genome. I tried uses liftOver function to convert my DMR chromosomal locations to older genome build but there are too many errors.

 My second question is 2) What does precedence means in annotateWithGeneParts? The percentage of promoters, exon, intron and intergenic regions differ if precedence is to True or False. Little bit of explanation beyond the meaning of the word would be helpful.

 Thank you,
Neel

On Sat, 2 Sep 2017 at 03:32, Neel Aluru <nal...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hello All,

 I am bit confused about the annotation function. I would really appreciate if someone can explain it to me.
 
 I am using annotateWithGeneParts to annotate the DMRs and using the gene IDs to do enrichment analysis. I have seen some published studies where GREAT (http://bejerano.stanford.edu/great/public/html/) is used to annoate and do the enrichment analysis. My question is 1) Are they both one and the same? The reason I am asking is I work with zebrafish and GREAT website still uses older genome. I tried uses liftOver function to convert my DMR chromosomal locations to older genome build but there are too many errors.

GREAT associations regions of interest differently please read their paper. Our annotation is purely based on if dmrs/dmcs overlap with genomic features such as promoter, exon and introns. We also don't provide gene id association, just statistics of how many regions of interest overlap with those features

My second question is 2) What does precedence means in annotateWithGeneParts? The percentage of promoters, exon, intron and intergenic regions differ if precedence is to True or False. Little bit of explanation beyond the meaning of the word would be helpful.

Precedence is used if a DMR/DMC is overlapping with multiple features. If it overlaps with a promoter and an exon we count it as if it only overlaps with the promoter if precedence is TRUE



 Thank you,
Neel
